hero.alt: A trilobite's calcite compound eye emerges from black Cambrian water as its facets catch the first thin beam of light.

glossary.name: Animal suffering
glossary.definition: Negative conscious experience in nonhuman creatures; not identical with death, injury, or nociception.

glossary.name: Nociception
glossary.definition: Neural detection and encoding of damaging or potentially damaging stimuli; it does not by itself prove felt pain.

glossary.name: Sentience
glossary.definition: Capacity for felt experience, including pain, pleasure, fear, comfort, or distress.

glossary.name: Natural selection
glossary.definition: Differential survival and reproduction associated with heritable variation; a process without foresight or moral intention.

glossary.name: Secondary causation
glossary.definition: The Catholic claim that creatures genuinely act as causes while depending at every moment upon God as first cause.

glossary.name: In statu viae
glossary.definition: In a state of journeying; creation's unfinished movement toward its appointed perfection.

glossary.name: Self-making creation
glossary.definition: Analogical shorthand for a world with lawful causal integrity and genuine developmental history, not conscious matter creating or choosing itself.

glossary.name: Natural evil
glossary.definition: Traditional term for suffering, death, disaster, and deprivation not directly caused by a morally culpable creature.

glossary.name: Privation
glossary.definition: Augustine and Aquinas's account of evil as the loss or corruption of a due good rather than a positive substance.

glossary.name: Evidential problem of evil
glossary.definition: The argument that the kinds, amounts, or distribution of suffering count probabilistically against a perfectly good and powerful God.

glossary.name: Theodicy and defense
glossary.definition: A theodicy proposes God's actual reasons for permitting evil; a defense more modestly shows how God and evil might be logically compatible.

glossary.name: Cosmic redemption
glossary.definition: Christian hope that salvation includes the transformation of material creation, not only human souls.

glossary.name: Eschatological hope
glossary.definition: Hope concerning creation's final fulfillment in God.

glossary.name: Animal resurrection
glossary.definition: The speculative hope that individual animals may be restored; not defined Catholic doctrine.

glossary.name: Charles Darwin
glossary.definition: Naturalist whose theory of evolution by natural selection sharpened the theological problem of apparently designed suffering.

glossary.name: William L. Rowe
glossary.definition: Analytic philosopher known for the evidential argument from a fawn's apparently pointless agony.

glossary.name: Paul Draper
glossary.definition: Philosopher who argues that the observed distribution of pain and pleasure is more expected under a hypothesis of indifference than under theism.

glossary.name: Augustine of Hippo
glossary.definition: Church Father associated with evil as privation and the beauty of the created order as a whole.

glossary.name: Thomas Aquinas
glossary.definition: Catholic theologian of primary and secondary causation, creaturely goods, providence, and classical eschatology.

glossary.name: C. S. Lewis
glossary.definition: Christian writer who treated animal pain directly, while marking many of his proposals as speculation.

glossary.name: John Hick
glossary.definition: Philosopher of soul-making theodicy, useful chiefly as a contrast because animals are not moral agents being formed through suffering.

glossary.name: Holmes Rolston III
glossary.definition: Environmental philosopher who describes evolutionary creation as tragic, prolific, and cruciform.

glossary.name: Christopher Southgate
glossary.definition: Theologian of evolutionary suffering, creaturely selving, divine co-suffering, and eschatological fulfillment.

glossary.name: David Bentley Hart
glossary.definition: Orthodox theologian who resists making every horror a necessary ingredient in a total providential calculus.

glossary.name: Pope Francis
glossary.definition: Author of Laudato Si', emphasizing each creature's own purpose and the universe's common destiny in the risen Christ.

visuals.title: The unwitnessed fawn
visuals.label: THE EVIDENTIAL PROBLEM
visuals.caption: The problem is not merely that suffering exists, but that it is ancient, specific, and felt by creatures who could not ask what it was for.
visuals.alt: A distant fawn stands small in a smoke-dark forest after a natural fire, surrounded by ash and fading ember haze.

visuals.title: The long dark before us
visuals.label: DEEP TIME
visuals.caption: The five great extinctions are not a proof by themselves; they make the age and scale of the question impossible to ignore.

visuals.title: Good, but not finished
visuals.label: IN STATU VIAE
visuals.caption: The first world is good; the last is glory; history is the journey between them.

visuals.title: The evolutionary forge
visuals.label: CREATURELY HISTORY
visuals.caption: The wolf and the deer write one another into being, but usefulness is not yet a moral receipt.
visuals.alt: A deer and wolf move around a central ring of fire, their forms partly composed of ancestral silhouettes and fossil traces.

visuals.title: The beautiful plate and the terrible life
visuals.label: NATURAL HISTORY
visuals.caption: Draftsmanship can make a system intelligible without making its suffering justified.
visuals.alt: A wasp, caterpillar, branching parasite form, and tumor-like growth arranged as a dreamlike natural-history plate on aged paper.

visuals.title: Job's procession
visuals.label: THE WILD GLORY
visuals.caption: The whirlwind does not give Job a tidy answer. It widens the field of what he must see before he speaks.
visuals.alt: A tiny human figure stands beneath a storm whirlwind surrounded by lion, raven, wild ass, ostrich, horse, hawk, eagle, and sea creatures.

visuals.title: Not one sparrow
visuals.label: BIRTH-PANGS
visuals.caption: The line of gold is not a diagram of providence. It is the faint possibility that no small life is outside God's notice.
visuals.alt: A small sparrow flies through near-black blue, intersected by one faint line of gold light.

visuals.title: Down into the food chain
visuals.label: THE LAMB
visuals.caption: The manger is an animal trough. The answer enters creation from below.
visuals.alt: An infant rests in an animal feeding trough in a cold stable, with straw, rough wood, and nearby animals in shadow.

visuals.title: The descent
visuals.label: FROM STARS TO CROSS
visuals.caption: The Christian claim is not that God watches the food chain from a safe height, but that he comes down into it.

visuals.title: The wounded resurrection
visuals.label: THE VICTIM ALIVE
visuals.caption: The scar remains visible; the wound is not denied, but it is no longer bleeding.
visuals.alt: The risen Christ's hand appears in dawn light with a closed scar, opening from tomb-darkness into a restored landscape.

visuals.title: Memory as ark
visuals.label: COSMIC REDEMPTION
visuals.caption: Perhaps God's memory is an ark: not a cage, but a field in which no creature's reality is discarded.
visuals.alt: Translucent extinct and living creatures gather within an ark-shaped field of light without cages or hierarchy of scale.

visuals.title: The fawn and the Lamb
visuals.label: THE LAST WORD
visuals.caption: The two images do not merge. Resurrection-gold crosses both without asking the fawn to become an argument.
visuals.alt: A solemn diptych places a small fawn in smoke and ember on one side and the wounded Lamb in a restored landscape on the other.

visuals.title: The roadside vigil
visuals.label: CODA
visuals.caption: No halo, no diagram, no explanation: one hand stays until the creature stops.
visuals.alt: At a dark roadside, one human hand rests gently on a deer's flank beside gravel, ditch grass, and a small hazard-amber glow.

pulls.quote: The blood is older than the sin.
pulls.label: THE ANTIQUITY OF SUFFERING

pulls.quote: Long before anyone could ask why, there were beings to whom something could happen badly.
pulls.label: THE QUESTION BEFORE HUMAN GUILT

pulls.quote: The world is made by God in such a way that it also genuinely makes history.
pulls.label: A WORLD WITH AN INSIDE

pulls.quote: The forge explains much and consoles nothing.
pulls.label: THE LIMIT OF EVOLUTIONARY EXPLANATION

pulls.quote: An alarm still ringing in a house that has already burned down and has nobody left in it to warn.
pulls.label: THE QUESTION OF USELESS PAIN

pulls.quote: He came down into the food chain.
pulls.label: THE DESCENT

pulls.quote: And he did not come in at the top.
pulls.label: THE LAMB

pulls.quote: It has to be the victim alive.
pulls.label: THE STANDARD OF VINDICATION

pulls.quote: Perhaps God's memory is an ark.
pulls.label: MEMORY AS PROMISE

pulls.quote: The scars of Christ do not say that crucifixion was harmless. They say that crucifixion failed.
pulls.label: THE LAST WORD

pulls.quote: Do not pretend to possess the fawn's receipt.
pulls.label: THE GOVERNING HUMILITY
